exercise.name: Farmer's Walk
library_steps: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand and stand tall.
Walk with short, quick steps, shoulders back and arms straight.
Bend your knees to set the weights down at the end.
exercise.one_line_summary: Walking tall with a heavy dumbbell hanging in each hand, arms straight, shoulders back, short steps. Picture 1: left foot forward, right foot pushing off; picture 2: the next step, right foot forward.

setup.target: One dumbbell per hand, equal weight, hanging at the sides, palms facing in.
setup.why: Library step; splitting the load evenly cut spine compression 44 % vs one hand at 30 kg (S2).

setup.target: Tall trunk, shoulders back (not shrugged up, not rounded), head level.
setup.why: Library step; the stiffened torso carries the load (S1).

setup.target: Short steps: about 0.3 m heel-to-toe-line between the feet.
setup.why: Library: short, quick steps keep the loads from swinging.

movement.start: ankle 0.15 m in front of the hip, foot flat, knee ~13 deg

movement.measure: ankle position / knee bend / heel lift
movement.start: ankle 0.17 m behind the hip, heel up ~15 deg on the ball of the foot, knee ~36 deg

movement.measure: elev (arm out from the side) / elbow
movement.start: 10 / 5 (arms straight, just clear of the thighs)

muscles.emg: Not measured in S1/S2 (torso and hip EMG only); S3 uses the carry to build grip
muscles.role: Holds the heavy dumbbells; library primary and what most people feel first.
Holds the shoulder girdle up against the pull of the weights; library primary.
muscles.surface: Top of the shoulders between neck and acromion.

muscles.emg: Measured in S1 events; with internal oblique, quadratus lumborum and adductors it holds the pelvis level in single-leg stance (S3 summarising S1)
muscles.role: Keeps the hips level each step.

muscles.emg: Abdominals peaked during the walking phase of the farmer's walk (S1); low (about 2-8 % MVC) with 10-30 kg split between both hands (S2)
Peaked during the lift-off, not the walk (S1)
muscles.surface: Either side of the lower spine.

muscles.role: Supports the pelvis in the frontal plane.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Shoulders up at the ears or rolled forward.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library cue: shoulders back, stand tall.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Trunk tips forward or to one side.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Raises spine load; the carry is meant to be done with a stiff, upright trunk.

sources.citation: McGill SM, McDermott A, Fenwick CMJ. 2009. Comparison of different strongman events: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load, and stiffness. J Strength Cond Res 23(4):1148-1161.
sources.what_it_gave: Farmer's walk with 75 kg per hand vs suitcase carries: 16-channel trunk/hip EMG; abdominals peaked while walking in the farmer's walk, low-back extensors at the lift; stiff torso supports the hips.

sources.citation: McGill SM, Marshall L, Andersen J. 2013. Low back loads while walking and carrying: comparing the load carried in one hand or in both hands. Ergonomics 56(2):293-302.
sources.what_it_gave: 6 men: 15 kg per hand = 1628 N L4/L5 vs 2874 N for 30 kg in one hand; trunk EMG 2-10 % MVC with loads split between hands.

sources.citation: McCall P. 2014. Strongman training for your clients. ACE ProSource.
sources.what_it_gave: Farmer's walk = a heavy object in each hand walked a set distance; grab the dumbbell end for more grip work; McGill's carries show internal oblique, quadratus lumborum, gluteus medius and adductor magnus keep the pelvis stable.

clip_check.check: Front foot flat, back foot on its ball (toes on the floor)
Step length (ankle to ankle, along the walk)
Arms straight, dumbbells clear of the thighs
Picture 2 is the mirror step (right foot forward)
Forearms and traps are the strongest red in both pictures
